title: PKS 1424−418: A persistent candidate source of the mm─γ-ray connection?
question: Is there a long-term correlation between mm (ALMA) and gamma-ray (Fermi-LAT) light curves of the FSRQ PKS 1424-418, with what time lag, and what does the mm spectral index say about jet opacity and the gamma-ray site

what.value: 4FGL catalog sources and their default spectral models, used for the LAT background model

evidence.quote: We kept the default spectral models provided by the catalog for all the sources except our target

what.value: Details of the ALMA calibrator catalog and its observations

evidence.quote: Details of the catalog and ALMA observations can be found in (cite: bonato2018).

what.value: Apparent jet speed beta_app = 9 (median for FSRQs)

evidence.loc: 4.3 Potential effects of a core shift to the gamma-ray origin
evidence.quote: a median value for FSRQs; (cite: weaver2022)

evidence.loc: 4.3 Potential effects of a core shift to the gamma-ray origin

recipe.goal: Build 6-day gamma-ray light curve from Fermi-LAT
recipe.method: Standard Fermi-LAT unbinned likelihood analysis of Pass 8 data in 6-day bins, power-law model for the target, two fits per bin with faint sources removed
key_parameters: ROI radius 10 deg; 4FGL sources within 20 deg included
SOURCE class evclass=128, FRONT+BACK evtype=3, zmax 90 deg
Upper limits for TS < 20 or dF/F >= 0.5; faint sources with TS < 9 removed before second fit
assumptions: Simple power law for the target; no significant difference from LogParabola

recipe.goal: Assemble ALMA band 3, 6 and 7 light curves
recipe.method: Take flux densities from the ALMA calibrator catalogue; average multiple measurements at the same timestamp; treat 91 and 103 GHz as 95 GHz band 3
key_parameters: Band 3 median sampling interval 6 days (average ~10 days)

recipe.goal: Pearson correlation between mm and gamma-ray light curves
recipe.method: Divide the full time range into equal-sized bins, average flux in each bin, correlate local means over overlapping bins; repeat over many bin sizes
key_parameters: 488 calculations with Bin_eq from 6 to 100 days

recipe.goal: Search for time delay with the LCCF and assess significance
recipe.method: Local cross-correlation function with 6-day delay bins between band 3 and gamma-ray light curves; confidence levels from 100,000 simulated gamma-ray light curves
key_parameters: Also tested delay bins of 12, 30 and 60 days
assumptions: Gamma-ray PSD as bending power law and PDF as gamma plus log-normal mixture; empty bins filled by linear interpolation

recipe.goal: Compute (sub)mm spectral index between band 3 and band 7
recipe.method: Spectral index alpha from binned band 3 (95 GHz) and band 7 (345 GHz) flux densities, uncertainty by error propagation
assumptions: alpha ~ -0.5 is the boundary between optically thick and thin

recipe.goal: Estimate LCCF peak lags with Gaussian fits for bands 3 and 7
recipe.method: Fit a single Gaussian to the central LCCF hump, using only points above the first side-lobe peak (LCCF ~0.48); delta t = 8 days for band 7

recipe.goal: Convert lags into deprojected distance between mm core and gamma-ray site
recipe.method: Distance from apparent jet speed, lag, viewing angle and redshift: delta d = beta_app c tau / (sin theta_jet (1+z))
assumptions: Higher beta_app gives a larger distance range (0.71-2.14 pc)

answer_key.quantity: Mean Pearson coefficient, band 3 vs gamma-ray (488 bin sizes)

evidence.quote: The r$_{\rm P}$ values are $\sim$0.76 on average, with a 1 $\sigma$ uncertainty of 0.02 (minimum and maximum of 0.71 and 0.86, respectively).

answer_key.quantity: LCCF peak value band 3 vs gamma-ray at tau = 0

evidence.quote: Only the top part of this central LCCF hump where it peaks at $\tau$ = 0 with LCCF $\sim$ 0.75, exceeds the confidence level of 99.9%.
with an uncertainty of $\pm$3 days from $\tau$ = 0

score_reason: Both data sets are public and the correlation, LCCF and spectral-index recipes are clearly described with numeric results, but software versions, catalogue selection, bin edges and fit details are missing.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA calibrator-catalogue and Fermi-LAT data, a mostly complete recipe, and numeric results (r_P ~0.76, LCCF peak ~0.75 at zero lag, mean alpha -0.57) that can be re-derived.
